original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: On the fixed eleven-wire F509 map of R439 phase-B block 509 (registers [17,22,33,38,50,60,67,77,87,92,468]), does the all-length inverse-column frame invariant force exceptional source 22 to exit on the full block frame, so that the original single-climb paid-frame invoice {2:7,3:2} is minimal for 0<a<1 under all legal replacement circuits with restored dirty inputs?
scope_change_reason: The drawn bit-mechanisms cards were overlapped: bit-new-register-model is covered by open PRs CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1414, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1491, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1495, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1496 and discussion 1317 claims, and bit-helper-contract's semantic-D H2/K question is covered by [PR1194](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1194)/PR1311 and adjacent work (as several prior sessions recorded). This scope takes the concrete open request in the handoffs thread (discussion 1166, the [PR1368](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1368) block-508/509 exception) and the open next question of [PR1511](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1511), which closes only B508/source 19: apply the same invariant to the separately pinned block-509 boundary. It is a boundary-obstruction question on the same R439 helper/source word, not a changed operation alphabet.
bottleneck_link: A scoped obstruction on the bit supplier: it forecloses one candidate paid-frame improvement route (lower-frame resynthesis of block 509) and completes the ten-block lower-frame question of [PR1368](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1368) in its stated model. It changes no selected moment; the selected assembly is complex-bound.
stop_rule: One bounded experiment: pin the block-509 boundary, compute the inverse column of source 22 and the forced-exit table, and either conclude the forced-exit/invoice result or record the exact obstruction. No synthesis search; one pivot maximum.
evidence: PASS_R439_F509_SOURCE22_DUAL_BARRIER: inverse column of source 22 has support [17,22,33,38,77,87,468] including full-frame labels S_17=S_468=F509, so all eleven exits are forced to F509; single-climb profile {2:7,3:2} (block moment 7*2^q+2*3^q) is minimal for 0<a<1, with unchanged continuation and literal inverse cleanup accounted. The pinned-word adapter binds the constants to SHA-256 e3e301e6... (B[283:314], 31 ADDs). 11 failure controls reject; 2,048-input fixture replay passes. Concurrent corroboration: discussion 1515 and [PR1535](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1535) answered the same question independently during this session; this package claims no priority and adds only an orientation control, the recorded continuation boundary (source 22 first reappears at C[293]), and a third independently written checker.
